clue.text: Part of Russia is revolting and reportedly less than sober

indicators.note: revolting here means turning over, so the little word is flipped end to end
reportedly tells us the next piece is a word as heard, not as written

parts.note: someone less than sober is beerier, more tipsy from beer

explanation.surface: A grumble that some Russian region is disgusting and its people are a bit drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like disgust but means turning over. 'reportedly' marks a sound-alike: beerier, said aloud, matches Stalin's police chief's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Siberia is the vast eastern region of Russia, so it is a part of that country.

clue.text: Butt and odd bits of belly in need of shave

parts.note: a butt, as of a cigarette, is a stub

indicators.note: the odd bits are the first, third and fifth letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A paunchy body part that needs a shave, butt and belly alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits of' takes letters 1, 3 and 5 of 'belly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stubbly chin has bristly regrowth, which is exactly when a person needs to shave.

clue.text: Lavatory fixtures in Spooner's telephone kiosk

indicators.note: Spooner's signals that the first sounds of two words are to be swapped

parts.note: to telephone someone is to call them
a kiosk, as a telephone kiosk, is a box

explanation.surface: Toilet fittings oddly located in a phone booth.
explanation.walkthrough: A telephone kiosk is a call box; swapping the opening sounds gives BALL COCKS. A ballcock is the float valve in a toilet cistern.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballcocks are the float-operated valves that refill a toilet cistern, standard plumbing in a lavatory.

clue.text: Customs of outspoken authors

indicators.note: outspoken here means spoken out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to author a book is to write it, so authors means writes

explanation.surface: The traditions of writers who speak their minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'authors' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Rites are ceremonial practices, the established customs of a community or faith.

clue.text: Dotty sat on wobbly ladder with leg on either side

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it
dotty means crazy, so the letters are jumbled
wobbly means unsteady, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A batty person perched on a shaky ladder, legs dangling either side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' rearranges SAT to AST; 'wobbly' rearranges LADDER to RADDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit astraddle is to straddle something, with one leg each side as on a horse.

clue.text: Surplus kept by Otto's parents

indicators.note: kept by means held within, so the letters lie inside these words

explanation.surface: Extra money that a boy's mother and father keep hold of.
explanation.definitionFit: Something to spare is extra, more than needed, which is a surplus.

clue.text: Fish head leaving terrible smell

indicators.note: head leaving means the first letter goes from the word

parts.note: a terrible smell is a stench

explanation.surface: A fish head gives off an awful stink.
explanation.definitionFit: The tench is a European freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Crooked partners, wife and husband, on board boat

indicators.note: on board means inside the vessel, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a skiff is a small light boat
in bridge East and West are partners

explanation.surface: A dishonest married couple on a boat, along with their partners.
explanation.walkthrough: EW is a bridge pairing: East and West play as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Skew-whiff is British slang for askew, not straight, which is crooked in the literal sense.

clue.text: Remove coat of most important foreigner

indicators.note: removing the coat strips off the outer layer, the first and last letters

parts.note: salient means most noticeable or important

explanation.surface: An instruction to take the coat off a very important foreign visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a person from another country, the legal term for a foreign national.

clue.text: Gracious, short lament over member of colony

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above the next piece
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: an elegy is a lament, a mournful poem
an ant lives in a colony

explanation.surface: A courteous brief mourning song for a colonist.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant and gracious both describe refined, stylish poise and good taste.

clue.text: Available to rent, ultimately you can still purchase it

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: An estate agent's line: a flat to let that you could also buy.
explanation.definitionFit: A property that is unlet has no tenant yet, so it is free to be rented.

clue.text: Soften up last pair of climate change deniers

indicators.note: last pair of takes the final two letters of the word
change signals the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Win over the last couple of people who deny climate change.
explanation.definitionFit: To tenderise meat is to soften it, by beating or marinating, before cooking.

clue.text: Left-leaning character is in favour of corporal punishment

parts.note: to back something is to be in favour of it
is shortens to 's
the lash is a whipping, a form of corporal punishment

explanation.surface: A left-wing figure who supports flogging.
explanation.walkthrough: The backslash is the keyboard symbol \ that leans to the left.
explanation.definitionFit: The backslash symbol slopes back to the left, so it is a typographic character that leans left.

clue.text: Money came first, introductions to grandees after

parts.note: to come first in a contest is to have won

indicators.note: introductions are the opening letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Cash triumphed first, with the bigwigs arriving later.
explanation.walkthrough: Wonga is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonga is informal British slang for cash, a colloquial word for money.

clue.text: Luxury purchase set back your old checking account

indicators.note: checking means holding back, so one piece stops the other inside it
set back means put in reverse order

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: An expensive buy that dented your former current account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' turns THY into YHT, which holds AC.
explanation.definitionFit: A yacht is a classic extravagance, a pleasure boat bought by the rich as a luxury.

clue.text: Steaming hot chocolate banishing depression and pain

indicators.note: steaming here means drunk, so the letters are thrown into disorder
banishing sends some letters away from the pool before it is reordered

parts.note: a col is a depression, a low pass between mountain peaks

explanation.surface: A hot sugary drink that cheers you up but leaves your teeth hurting.
explanation.walkthrough: Take C, O, L from the letters of HOT CHOCOLATE and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothache is a specific kind of pain, an ache in or around a tooth.

clue.text: Awkward end of Edward II, impaled by fellows and followers

indicators.note: this word only joins the neighbouring pieces: it says which one stands next to which in the answer
end of picks the last letter of the word
impaled by means pierced through, so this piece goes inside

parts.note: F is fellow, doubled for the plural
a cult is a group of devoted followers

explanation.surface: The grim death of King Edward II, said to have been impaled.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward II was reputedly killed with a red-hot poker, which gives the surface its grisly picture; here the Roman numerals are the pierced piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Difficult and awkward both describe something hard to handle or deal with.

clue.text: Motor sport is brilliant source of status for shady character

parts.note: Formula One, written F1, the 1 read as I
something that is brilliant shines

indicators.note: source of takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Formula racing gives glamorous status to a dodgy type.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishiness is suspiciousness; something fishy is shady, so it is a shady quality or character.

clue.text: In gainful work, for sure

indicators.note: work as a verb means knead or shape, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone who is definitely in paid employment.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfailing means reliable, never letting you down, which is to be sure or certain.

clue.text: Pet bears hang about for pieces of cake

indicators.note: bears means carries or holds, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: a puss is a pet cat
to hover is to hang about in one place

explanation.surface: Pets loiter around hoping for slices of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of cake is something easy, and pushovers are easy tasks or easily beaten opponents.

clue.text: Rampage antisocially over parade

indicators.note: the letters run over the gap between these two words

explanation.surface: Rioters run wild in an antisocial way and break up a procession.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a public spectacle or procession, which can be a parade.

clue.text: Couple short of place fit to accommodate fine horse

indicators.note: to accommodate means to take in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A spot just right for stabling a fine horse.
explanation.walkthrough: In racing a place usually means the top three; finishing fifth is a couple of positions short.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse finishing fifth misses third, the last placed position, by two places.

clue.text: Sackcloth and ashes in Barking

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters go crazy

explanation.surface: Penitents in sackcloth and ashes in the London district of Barking.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is also a district of east London; the biblical sackcloth and ashes are signs of mourning.
explanation.definitionFit: Hessian is coarse jute or hemp fabric, the material used for sacks, so sackcloth.

clue.text: Talked about origin of hunger strike together

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to sing to the police is to talk, so talked is sang

indicators.note: origin of takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Discussing the start of a hunger strike among protesters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talked about' looks like a sound signal; 'Talked' is SANG, slang for informing, and 'about' reverses it to GNAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnash the teeth is to grind or strike them together in anger.

clue.text: An absorbing review of unusual peripheral

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so this piece encloses the next
review here means look back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: odd means unusual

explanation.surface: A gripping critique of some strange computer gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer peripheral, like a printer, is an extra device, an add-on to the main machine.

clue.text: Reposing, I rearranged flimsy clothes

indicators.note: rearranged plainly says the letters are put into another order

explanation.surface: Lying back, I changed into something light and sheer.
explanation.definitionFit: Peignoirs are light, loose dressing gowns worn by women, typically of sheer fabric.

clue.text: Extremes of polar cold costing one dear

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: icy means very cold

explanation.surface: Polar expeditions in biting cold cost someone a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pricy is expensive, and what costs you dear costs a great deal.

clue.text: Are you texting to support rising female Indian leader?

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below
rising in a down clue means reading upwards, so reversed

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
in text speak are you is written R U

explanation.surface: A message asking whether you'll back an up-and-coming woman leading India.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first prime minister, a famous national leader.

clue.text: Extra ingredient contains cocaine, getting people hooked

indicators.note: contains means holds inside, so the second piece goes within

parts.note: an additive is an extra ingredient
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: A drug-laced additive that gets people hooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something addictive causes dependence, getting its users hooked on it.

clue.text: Regularly cut wheat in this country

indicators.note: regularly cut means every other letter is removed, keeping the alternate ones

explanation.surface: Wheat is harvested at set intervals in this land.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the even letters of WHEAT IN THIS gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is a Caribbean nation sharing the island of Hispaniola, an independent country.

clue.text: Judge admits princess hides here

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it
Anne is Britain's Princess Royal

explanation.surface: A judge lets in a princess who is hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: A tannery is where animal hides are treated into leather, so a place hides are found.

clue.text: Weapon wounded left-wingers of unimpeachable niceness

parts.note: to be stung is to be hurt or wounded

indicators.note: the left wing of a word is its first letter, so take the opening letters

explanation.surface: Left-wing politicians of perfect decency hurt by a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A stun gun is an electroshock device used to incapacitate, a type of weapon.
